findings.description: The reports_archive bucket defines no server_side_encryption_configuration block, so objects such as the vendor roster seed object are stored using S3's unconfigured default with no customer-managed KMS key and no enforceable at-rest encryption control.
The ledger_exports bucket contains financial ledger data but declares no server_side_encryption_configuration, leaving export objects without an enforced encryption-at-rest configuration.
The ops_runbooks bucket stores operational runbooks and has no server_side_encryption_configuration block, so its contents are not covered by an enforced encryption-at-rest setting.

The model_artifacts bucket is versioned and logged but declares no server_side_encryption_configuration, so model artifacts and their retained versions are not protected by an enforced at-rest encryption configuration.

The bucket that receives server access logs from model_artifacts is configured with the legacy canned ACL 'log-delivery-write'. This grants WRITE and READ_ACP to the global LogDelivery group rather than to a narrowly scoped logging principal, enabling any account's logging service to write objects into the audit bucket and overwrite access-log evidence. It also relies on a deprecated ACL-based access model rather than bucket-owner-enforced ownership and policy.

With force_destroy = true and a writable log-delivery ACL, the audit trail bucket holding access-log evidence can be destroyed along with all objects, undermining the integrity and non-repudiability of the audit record. Audit stores should be deletion-protected (e.g. Object Lock / MFA delete style controls) rather than destroyable.

The audit bucket itself has no access logging of its own and no policy restricting the log-delivery principal, so reads and deletes of audit objects are not themselves auditable — a gap in defence in depth for the most security-sensitive store in the account.
force_destroy = true on reports_archive means a single erroneous or malicious Terraform apply deletes every object in the bucket, including the seeded vendor roster, without any retention guard.
force_destroy = true on the ledger export bucket allows all financial export objects to be irreversibly deleted during destroy or replacement, removing any retention safeguard on regulated data.
force_destroy = true on model_artifacts permits mass deletion of all model artifact versions, removing the ability to roll back to a previously trusted model.
force_destroy = true on ops_runbooks allows all runbook content to be destroyed on a single apply, removing operational and incident-response documentation.

The seed object is written to reports_archive, which has no encryption configuration and the object itself specifies no server_side_encryption, so the vendor roster is stored without an enforced encryption-at-rest setting.
